en: Emergency! I repeat: we\nhave an emergency!
Disengaging warp drive!
What's going on?
The sensors have picked\nup on a large <font color=yellow>belt of\ndebris</font> up ahead.
I have stopped the ship,\nsince traveling any further\ncould prove dangerous.

In fact, had I waited even
a fraction of a second
longer, we would be space
dust right now.
I am so glad I noticed in\ntime...
As am I... I don't fancy the\nidea of being laid to rest\nin the rubble before us.
Indeed. Even just the\nthought makes me\nshudder.
So what now? Should we\ntake a detour?
That was what I was\nhoping to do but...
With our current sensors I\nam unable to see where\nthe belt ends.

Oh dear, oh dear. What
are we to do? If we were
to re-engage the warp
drive we will no doubt
collide with the debris...

Perhaps if we were to
follow the perimeter of the
belt we would eventually
be able to find where it
ends and emerge from the
other side...

We cannot discount the
possibility, however, that it
runs on forever. Perhaps
the ultimate solution would
be for us to return to the
star we initially―

Captain! You cannot be
serious. To attempt to
navigate our way through
the debris would be akin
to suicide!
Even with nine lives we\nwould still likely perish!
...If you truly believe you\nare capable of such a\nfeat, then I shall trust you.
Besides, all the other\nalternatives are equally, if\nnot more, unappealing.
Are the both of you\nabsolutely sure you want\nto do this?
Well, we once made it\nthrough space without any\nshields, didn't we?
If we managed that, we\ncan do anything.
I must admit that was one\nof my more impressive\naccomplishments!

I cannot tell you how
overjoyed I am to hear
that I have won your trust
and that you would place
your lives in my hands!

Very well! I shall do
everything in my power to
once again achieve a
miracle! I will part this sea
of debris and open up a
path to salvation!
I don't think that's how it\nworks...
Do not worry! Do not fret!\nI shall take care of\neverything!
If you say so...

(I shall keep my comments
to myself for now. If Coro
were to become
distressed at this juncture
it could cause us even
more problems.)

Full speed ahead, my
friends! Leave it to me―I
will get us across this
death trap alive!
I am picking up on a pulse\nup ahead!

What? You mean to say
there's a shipwreck
survivor amongst the
rubble!? We must help
them!
I do not think it is a\nperson...
Then what is it?
A moment if you would.
I found it!

According to the
information available in my
database, there is a type
of creature known to
inhabit areas with a high
concentration of debris.

They evolved within these
belts and live by
consuming rubble such as
the boulders and metals
present here.

I cannot say I am
surprised. Space is filled
with a variety of strange
specimens.

We are in trouble. The
creature will see this ship
as a potential source of
food...
You think it will attack us?

There is a good possibility
of it. And when it does, it
will latch onto and melt
through the hull of the
ship.

Even if we were to try and
make our way through the
debris at top speed, it will
catch up to us in no time.
We have no choice―we\nmust eliminate this beast.
Perhaps there is\nsomething among the\ndebris that can save us.
Do ships taste that good?

To think that you would go
out of your way to kill this
monster and make my job
of steering the ship
easier. You are a
hero―nay, god!
I was not aware you\nbelieved in the existence\nof a higher power...
I do not. I am a robot,\nafter all.

Ah, I nearly forgot you,
too, were fond of ghosts
and treasure... With this
creature on the loose,
there should no shortage
of phantom ships and
riches nearby.

From what I have been
able to see, there are no
phantom ships around
us―only debris!

We are traversing through
a virtual graveyard of
them! All these floating
parts once belonged to a
vessel.

I refuse to believe that!
We are flying amongst
rubble...n-not the remains
of ships.

While I cannot vouch for
the taste, iron is an
extremely important
source of nutrition for
these creatures.

If you are interested in
taking a bite of our ship,
however, we would first
need to construct a set of
steel teeth.

Supplementary gear to
strengthen your bones
and the muscles in your
face is also a must!

And for the ultimate dining
experience, we need to
think of how to season
the ship! I am thinking a
bit of banana on top
would add a nice layer of
flavor.
Now is not the time for\nthis nonsense!

Let us put all thoughts
except for defeating the
enemy aside for now. If we
don't hurry we'll end up
that thing's dinner!
Captain, come! We must\ngo out there and face it\nhead-on.

I have confirmed the
presence of vital signs
and found the beasts in
my database, so I know
they exist...

But even after seeing
them with my own eyes, I
still cannot suppress my
disbelief.

I am just glad we were
able to defeat that beast...
Are there a lot these
creatures inhabiting this
area?

From what I understand
these creatures have high
reproduction rates and a
great deal of vigor.

Similar to cockroaches,
seeing one of them means
there are 30 more lurking
nearby.
So this belt is a hideout of\nsorts for these beasts.
That would be correct...

That you should volunteer
to kill all of them for
us―you are far too kind,
Captain!

And to repay such
kindness I shall do
everything in my power to
improve the steering of
this ship!
Captain, up ahead! Look\nclosely at that debris.
It is the remnants of a\nship...
Yes, but you are missing\nthe point. I found this\ninside!
What is it?
You do not recognize this\nitem?
Exactly! It very closely\nresembles a pulse tower\nenergy unit.
Now that you mention it, I\nsee the similarities.
Captain, we must look into\nthis.

If that truly is an energy
unit, then there is a
chance that the wreckage
was once a Purge ship.

Indeed. Investigating it
could yield us a lot of
clues. So will you be off,
then?
Welcome back! How did\nyour explorations go?

So, it was as we
suspected―the wreckage
is that of a former Purge
ship.

Of that there is no doubt.
We even saw the exact
same emblem as that
which is inscribed inside
pulse towers.
Then we can say with\nabsolute certainty it\nbelonged to them.

I tried to gather what data
I could find amongst the
remains but I am not sure
how much of it has
actually survived.
Allow me to check. Please\nstandby.
This looks like the\ncaptain's logbook.
The data is so corrupted, I\ncan barely decipher any of\nit.
That is a true shame...

You want to remove the
portions that are not easy
to hear and then play it?
Let me see...
The CS...it...Operation:\nFrost is...divide light and\ndark...
Levara...is...for the\nOperation: Frost...
Whoever this is seems to\nmake great mention of the\nOperation: Frost.
I wonder if they were\nsomeone deeply involved\nin this scheme...

...This scheme that was
also mentioned in the
recording we found on
Planet Pasithee.
Yes, it would seem that\nway.

All we can say for sure at
this juncture is that the
wreckage is somehow
related to the Operation:
Frost and the Purge.

Of that there is no doubt.
The question is, what
exactly is this Operation:
Frost?

Considering the frequency
with which that word was
used, we can surmise it is
rather important. Sadly,
we still have little
information beyond that...
The fact that we found\none Purge ship means\nthere might be more.

Understood. If I detect
any other ships with the
aforementioned emblem, I
will report it to you
immediately.
Professor, we have a\nproblem!
...Er, that is not what I\nmeant to say.
Father!
...Wrong again.
Captain! Ah, yes, Captain!
What's wrong now?
I found it! Detected it!\nUncovered it!
I have spied a ship with\nthe Purge emblem on it.
Excellent work!

There is a good possibility
we will find nothing in the
wreckage, but it would be
foolish of us to not at
least check.
The emblem was a hoop\nsnake right?
Yes, it was, and soon\nenough we will be entering\nthe snake's den.

When I was younger, my
brother and I would make
bold declarations like that
and then venture outside
to play explorers.
Ah, the nostalgia...
To think that you were\nonce so young and\ncarefree...

Captain, indeed! By the
sound of it, Eve's
memories are returning to
her!

Eve, if we were to delve
into this memory perhaps
we can learn more about
your past and where you
are from!

That is the extent of what
I remember. Besides, I do
not think this particular
memory will yield any
clues regarding my home
planet.
Very well...

There may be some tidbits
hidden away in the
recesses of your mind. If
you ever recall something,
however small, do be sure
to inform us.
Thank you.
Now, let us re-focus on\nthe task at hand!

Hopefully exploring the
remains of this Purge ship
will reveal some important
clues to us.
You are back! How did\nyour search go?
So you were unable to\nfind any new information?

Unfortunately there was
nothing of value inside,
since it appeared to
simply be a transport ship.
A transport ship?
If only the ship it was\nprotecting was still there...
...We might have been able\nto learn more.

The fact that they sent a
defense ship to protect
the transport ship means
it was transporting
something very important.
Precisely!

The Purge's place of
residence, who they are,
or what their aim is...we
know next to nothing
about this organization.

All we have been able to
confirm is that they
created Operation: Frost
and are somehow related
to pulse towers that
produce rare metals.

If only we were able to
understand the meaning
behind these things, we
would be a step closer to
finding the Purge.

Very well. I shall
recalibrate the sensors to
project horizontally to
expand our view of the
debris.
Just make sure you don't\ncrash us.
Could it be? Is it\npossible? Might it be\ntrue?

Perhaps that emblem is
not what we think it is. Oh,
but if I say something and
am wrong I will surely get
yelled at...

In fact, Eve would likely go
so far as to erase my
video compilation of the
Captain as retribution!
That just will not do!
Did you discover\nsomething?
Coro! Be careful! You're\ngoing to crash us!
...Why do you have a video\ncompilation of me?
Y-yes, I think I did! I\nstumbled across it on\naccident.
Simmer down. When you\nget flustered it's hard to\ntalk to you.
Ack! To the right!\nChanging course to the\nright!
Phew... That could have\nended badly.
Thank the heavens we are\nsomehow still alive.
The answer to that should\nbe obvious!

When we finally return to
Earth, I am going to make
and sell a documentary of
all your extraordinary
exploits!

I have so much good
footage of you―everything
from you standing
triumphant on the
battlefield to you doing
everyday things like
showering and sleeping!

Captain, once you're back
on Earth I would suggest
pressing charges against
Coro for invasion of
privacy.

Returning to the topic at
hand, I discovered
something that might be
of interest―a transport
ship!

If I am right, we might be
able to get our hands on
some important
information.

Damage to the ship
appears to be minimal so
there is a good chance a
lot of the remaining
evidence has survived.
Captain, I am counting on\nyou to bring back some\nuseful information!
There!!!
Right there! That is a\npulse tower\ncounter-jamming device!
That must mean there\nare a lot of different items\nand devices onboard.
That would seem to be\nthe case.
Excellent eye, Captain! It\ndoes appear to be a pulse\ntower control unit.
If we charged it, do you\nthink it would still work?
Let us try and see!
It appears to be\nworking...but what do we\ndo from here?
Captain, if you would be\nso kind, might you connect\nit to the Quad Scanner?
I will attempt to operate\nit from here.
Captain!!! I got it to work!
Good job.
I was able to extract\ninformation regarding the\n<font color=yellow>Levarance language</font>.
Brilliant!
And how significant is this\nfinding?
It is wonderful!\nExceptional! Perhaps even\ngroundbreaking!

With this information I
might even be able to
analyze the <font color=yellow>data</font> we
obtained previously.
Are you referring to the\ndata we found on <font color=yellow>Maere</font>?
If so, that is fantastic\nnews!

Yes. I will begin looking
over the data posthaste. I
believe I will be able to
report back to you with
my findings shortly.

We'll be looking forward to
it. In the meantime, I'm
going to turn this device
off and return to the ship.
Safe travels, my friends.
Emergency! Emergency!\nEmergency!
Everything is an\nemergency with you. What\nis it this time?
Please look ahead. That\nrubble is flying straight\ntowards us!
Why don't you maneuver\nthe ship out of its path?
Because it is flying\nstraight toward us.
So steer around it!
I cannot do that because\nit is flying straight at us!

Is there something wrong
with your CPU!? What
you're saying makes
absolutely no sense!
There is not much I can\ndo if the rubble is intent\non pursuing us...
Pursuing us!?
That is what I have been\nsaying this entire time.
Surely you could have\npicked a less confusing\nway to phrase it!

...That said, I should
probably also apologize
for my earlier choice of
words.
According to the sensors,\nvital signs are emanating\nfrom the rubble's interior.
It appears the creature is\nsomehow manipulating the\ndebris.

Engaging the warp drive in
this belt to escape is not
an option, and if that thing
hits us we will be in big
trouble...
You want me to steer the\nship next to the\nmeteoroid!? But why!?
You are going to jump\nonto it and kill whatever is\ninside!?
While this does seem\nrather reckless, I shall do\nas you wish...

I will not be able to keep
the ship abreast the flying
rock for long, so be
prepared to jump as soon
as I pull up beside it!
Perfect! Wonderful!\nBrilliant! The meteoroid\nhas stopped moving!

Yes. As we suspected,
that beast you killed was
the rubble's source of
movement.
Thankfully it is now dead,\nand we are nearly out of\nthe belt!

We must proceed
cautiously until the end
lest we undo all our hard
work until now.
We made it! We are out of\nthe belt!
Good job, everyone. That\nwas some good navigation\nwork.

Thank you. I think every
family would be better off
with one of me in their
household!
I wouldn't be so sure\nabout that...
How rude!

One thousand years from
now I am going to be the
symbol of beauty. There
will not be a single person
who would not want me!
A thousand years...? That\nis quite far away, isn't it?

Since I wanted everyone
to concentrate on making
it through the belt, I did
not say anything earlier...

...But I have finished
analyzing the Purge's data
and have something very
important to share with
you.

Are you referring to the
indecipherable data we
obtained on Maere? What
did you learn from it?
Yes. It contains\ninformation about the CS\nplan.
So you've discovered the\ndetails of the plan!?
Yes, I did.
The plan designated\n"Operation: Frost" was of\ntruly monstrous scope.
What is that?

It seems they supercooled
their own planet, instantly
putting the whole planet
and its people into a
cryogenic state.
Cryogenic state!? The\nwhole planet!? That's\ninsanity!
Why would they do such a\nthing!?

The data did not include
any details on the reason
as to why or how they
enacted this plan.

They did, however, make
mention of a method that
could be employed to
obtain the rare metals
used for pulse towers.
These rare metals are\nsupposedly used to\nsupercool planets.

I recall the guerilla
members on Farbrooke
mentioning something
along those lines, and that
rare metals can fetch
hefty prices.
What I don't understand,\nhowever, is why would\nanyone want to do that?

True, just the fact that we
now know what the
Operation: Frost is, is
huge progress.

Shall we travel to the next
star system? I have
finished calculating the
route there.
Yes, let us be on our way.

It is our duty to do all in
our power to reduce the
number of people that fall
victim to the Purge's plan.

You have discovered a
New Route. You can now
choose this New Route
from the Select Planet
screen.
